newsitem.title: UK: Zinc prices to peak at $1,650 in 98 - Metal Bulletin.
newsitem.headline: Zinc prices to peak at $1,650 in 98 - Metal Bulletin.

text.p: Growth in Western world zinc consumption will resume in 1997, kicking off several years of expansion and pushing the stock/consumption ratio to critical levels, Metal Bulletin Research said in a report.
At the same time, prices will march higher as investment funds pile into the market, peaking at over $1,650 basis LME cash, in 1998.
LME three months ended the afternoon kerb on Friday at $1,169.
"The stock consumption ratio forecast for 1998 should dip below the level recorded in the bull market of 1988/89, when stocks represented 5.1 weeks demand," the report said.

"Against this background our base case price forecasts can be seen as conservative. Although we expect prices to peak at over $1,650 a tonne in 1998, this is still well below previous market peaks," it added.
Prices would end 1997 at around $1,425 per tonne and will average $1,288, about 25 percent up on the average for 1996.
Consumption should rise by 2.7 percent both this year and next, while refined production is seen increasing by 2.5 percent this year and by 3.8 percent in 1998, the report said.
Exports from the China and the Commonwealth of Independent States are expected to rise, it added.
By the end of 1997, the stocks-to-consumption ratio should stand at around six weeks, which would be the lowest level since 1989.

"If we assume that producer and consumer stocks are close to minimum levels, and therefore the stock draw down forecast for this year takes place at LME warehouses, then LME inventories would represent 2.6 weeks' consumption at the end of 1997," it said.
Normally the market needs a total reported stock level of under seven weeks or an LME stock level of under four weeks to allow a move in prices over $1,100 per tonne, Metal Bulletin said.
